samples.summary: The new access-log redaction covers only one path-borne credential (`/share-links/:token/resolve`); the workspace invite route `POST /invites/:token/accept` puts an equally grant-bearing token in the path and is left unredacted — and, being a mutation, it is logged at `info` on every success, not just on 4xx.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.controller.ts:117 — `@Post('invites/:token/accept')` with `@Param('token') token: string`; `workspaceService.acceptInvite(token, …)` grants workspace membership. `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` (packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts:79) lists only `['share-links','*','resolve']`, and `SENSITIVE_PARAMS` only ever sees the query string, so the invite token reaches the log verbatim. `customLogLevel` in packages/backend/src/app.module.ts:56-60 puts every non-GET at `info`, so this is logged on the normal path. Fix belongs in `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS`.

samples.summary: `packages/backend/README.md` still documents the old `/auth/github` contract — no OAuth `state`, no CLI consent interstitial, no `?nonce`/`?code_challenge` requirement, no `400` on plain-http non-loopback origins, and no `FRONTEND_URL/login?error=login_state` failure redirect. The design docs under docs/design were updated; this consumer-facing README was not.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/README.md:191-192 — `| GET | /auth/github | - | Initiate GitHub OAuth flow |` and README.md:397-403 describing the old five-step flow, versus the new contract in packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:287-360 and docs/design/backend.md:103-162.

samples.summary: CLI login now hard-fails (`400 Command-line sign-in requires an https server`) on any self-hosted deployment served over plain http on a non-loopback host, but the user-facing self-hosting / CLI docs still show a plain-http setup and an unqualified `wafflebase login`. Existing self-hosters on http lose CLI login with no documented remedy.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:294-299 throws `BadRequestException` when `cliLoginAvailable()` is false, which is keyed on `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` scheme/loopback. packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42 configures `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL=http://localhost:3000/...` and packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:22/30 document `wafflebase login` with no scheme requirement. Only docs/design/cli.md:268 records the restriction.
searchedFor: read docs/design/cli.md around the CLI login section

samples.summary: The new failure redirect builds `${FRONTEND_URL}/login?error=…` from the origin alone, but the frontend router supports a deployment base path (`VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME`). Where a basename is set and `FRONTEND_URL` is the bare origin, a refused browser callback lands outside the SPA's routes instead of on the login page that now renders the `?error=` banner.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/App.tsx:76 — `<Router basename={import.meta.env.VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME}>` with `<Route path="/login" …>` at App.tsx:81; the backend composes the target at packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:357-361 with no knowledge of that basename. Confirming needs a deployment that sets VITE_FRONTEND_BASENAME while FRONTEND_URL omits the same prefix.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS (log-safe-url.ts:75-79) holds exactly one rule, ['share-links','*','resolve']; redactPathSecrets only rewrites paths matching a rule shape, and redactParams is applied only to the query substring (line 163), so SENSITIVE_PARAMS can never see a path segment. workspace.controller.ts:117 exposes POST /invites/:token/accept, and workspace.service.ts:152-206 turns that path segment into workspace membership (and leaves the token reusable, line 166-169), so it is a live grant-bearing credential. The route is reached from production frontend code (packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:156), and app.module.ts:56-60 assigns every non-GET a level of info, so the token is written verbatim to the access log on the normal success path, not just on 4xx. Repo-wide grep for redact|logSafeUrl|setGlobalPrefix|useLogger|pinoHttp found no other sanitisation layer, no global prefix, and no alternate invite-token redaction; app.module.ts:78-85 redact.paths covers only headers. No counterexample exists.
